headline: Soleno deal lifts revenue, squeezes near-term profit
summary_short: Revenue rose to $959M (+39.5% y/y, +17.7% q/q) on CRENESSITY and INGREZZA growth plus the newly-acquired VYKAT XR; diluted EPS fell to $1.39 from $1.91 last quarter as one-time Soleno acquisition costs weighed on margins.
summary_long: Net product sales grew on CRENESSITY's continued ramp, INGREZZA volume and record new-patient prescriptions, and the addition of VYKAT XR following the May 2026 acquisition of Soleno. Cost of revenues rose on higher royalties and VYKAT XR inventory step-up amortization. SG&A rose to 45.8% of revenue (from 41.6%) on continued commercial investment plus $96.8M of Soleno acquisition-related costs, including $40.2M of accelerated stock-based compensation; combined with $33.1M of separate transaction costs, these one-offs drove operating income and diluted EPS down sequentially despite the revenue gain. R&D rose on Phase 3 progression of osavampator and direclidine. No forward financial guidance was disclosed in the filing. Cash and equivalents rose to $332.4M; shareholders' equity grew to $3,693.6M.

drivers.explanation: Revenue growth from CRENESSITY, INGREZZA, and the newly-added VYKAT XR was partly offset sequentially by one-time Soleno acquisition costs (transaction costs, accelerated stock comp, inventory step-up), which compressed operating income and EPS versus Q1.

Increase primarily reflected increased net product sales of CRENESSITY, increased INGREZZA sales driven by volume growth in total prescriptions and record new prescriptions, and the inclusion of VYKAT XR sales following the Soleno acquisition.

Cost of revenues increase reflected higher net product sales, increased CRENESSITY royalties, $3.0M of VYKAT XR inventory fair-value step-up amortization, and $2.0M of Soleno acquisition-related expenses.

SG&A rose on commercial team expansion plus $96.8M of Soleno acquisition-related expenses (incl. $40.2M accelerated stock comp); combined with $33.1M of separate transaction costs, this outweighed revenue growth q/q.

Sequential decline traces to the same one-time Soleno acquisition and transaction costs cited for operating income, only partly offset by a lower effective tax rate (11.0% vs 32.6% a year ago) from foreign tax effects and R&D credits.
